problem: Existing 3D scene graph systems need depth sensors or calibrated cameras and complex pipelines, and they fix object/region granularity at mapping time or require a predefined task list. Their geometric room clustering also assumes structured indoor scenes.
motivation: A robot's tasks evolve during operation and need different granularity (whole stove for navigation, knobs for manipulation). Geometric foundation models make monocular reconstruction plug-and-play, but they have not been extended to hierarchical, task-driven scene graphs.
key_idea: Build a scene graph on VGGT-SLAM 2.0 from an uncalibrated monocular camera, storing keyframe-level CLIP embeddings as a visual memory so objects and regions are formed at query time at the task's granularity, with the places layer coming from a ground-segmentation head on GFM tokens.
insight: Deferring instance formation to query time (whole-keyframe embeddings, then SAM3) avoids committing to a granularity and removes tracking and association. On Clio it raises IoU to 0.37/0.28/0.30, versus 0.26/0.19/0.17 for Bayesian Fields. Intermediate GFM layers (layer 17 for VGGT, 13 for DA3) segment ground best, and about 300 annotated samples generalize indoors and outdoors. The per-place vMF statistic beats view averaging on region labelling (Acc 78.05 vs 73.93 for HOV-SG).
method: Geometric mapping: VGGT-SLAM 2.0 submaps of 16 keyframes chained by SL(4) factor-graph optimization; VGGT is the default GFM and DA3 variants are drop-in replacements; optional voxel sparsification keeps only queried objects dense.

Visual memory: one Perception Encoder CLIP embedding per keyframe. A text query is scored by cosine similarity, then top keyframes go to SAM3 while the camera frustum has not already seen a mapped instance of that query, so multiple instances are recovered. Masks are back-projected with depth.
Cached memory: resolved objects are stored as point clouds with oriented 3D bounding boxes. Later queries hit the cache first and fall back to visual memory.

Places layer: a convolutional ground-segmentation head on intermediate GFM tokens is trained on about 300 samples. Ground points are fitted with a plane and binned into tiles, with partial-boundary tiles and tiles under furniture removed. Tiles form a deformable graph with Dijkstra planning.

Regions layer: each place stores a von Mises-Fisher summary (mean direction, concentration kappa) of the keyframe embeddings that observe it. A query gives score kappa*<mu,q>, which is smoothed by confidence-aware label propagation over the places graph. A 2-component GMM thresholds the scores, and connected components above a minimum size become regions.

Agentic comprehension: an LLM agent calls object and region query tools. It searches exhaustively via SAM3, can detect an object's absence, and incrementally builds a task-specific scene graph in the cache.
Closed-vocabulary adaptation for the HOV-SG benchmark: per-category scoring with normalization, BFS label propagation for dense coverage, and Louvain community relabelling.

setting.backbone: VGGT (default) or Depth Anything 3 as GFM, with a trained ground-segmentation head; Perception Encoder CLIP, SAM3, and GPT-4o-mini agent (all frozen)
setting.training_data: Only the ground-segmentation head is trained, on about 300 annotated samples; everything else is training-free with pretrained foundation models.
setting.observation: uncalibrated monocular RGB video (GT depth and poses used in the Clio and SG3D quantitative evaluations)
setting.action_space: not applicable (mapping and querying); path planning by Dijkstra over the places graph
setting.simulator: HM3D-SEM scenes (SG3D and HOV-SG benchmarks), Clio datasets, real-world videos
setting.privileged: GT poses and depth for Clio and SG3D evaluations; the HOV-SG region benchmark is evaluated given GT region segmentation for semantic accuracy

numbers.extra: GT poses and depth given to all methods; prompts modified (no 'get', added 'pile of')

numbers.eval_set_note: 8 HM3D-SEM validation scenes, 1000 queries per scene
numbers.extra: GT poses and depth from the benchmark dataset
numbers.evidence: Table 2 sequential task grounding: FOUND-IT (Ours) + GPT-4o-mini 39.7 / 19.0

numbers.extra: adapted to closed vocabulary (Louvain etc.); Acc evaluated given GT region segmentation

numbers_note: Not a navigation-benchmark paper; metrics are mapping/grounding. Timing: about 6 fps with VGGT and 7 fps with DA3-LARGE on a 3090; 4 Hz on Jetson Thor.
results: On Clio, FOUND-IT is the only method that is best on all scenes and metrics, with IoU 0.37/0.28/0.30 vs Bayesian Fields' 0.26/0.19/0.17. On SG3D task grounding it reaches s-acc 39.7 and t-acc 19.0 vs DAAAM's 22.2 and 11.2 (about 79% higher s-acc). On HOV-SG rooms it gets Acc 78.05, 4.12 above HOV-SG. It runs real-time on a Spot-mounted Jetson Thor.
limitations: Failure of the geometric foundation-model mapping propagates to the scene graph.
Traversability and regions require keyframes that observe the floor.
